hook: Dive to the bottom of a swimming pool and your ears ache. Push a thumbtack and it slides into a wall, though you could never push your thumb in. Both come down to the same quantity, pressure: how much force is spread over how much area, and how it grows as you go deeper in a fluid.

prereq.why: Mass has a size but no direction.

prereq.q: A 2.0 kg book rests on a table. Near Earth's surface (g = 9.8 N/kg), the force of the table on it is
prereq.why: Equilibrium: the normal force balances the weight, mg = 19.6 N.

figure.caption: Pressure at a point acts equally in every direction and grows with depth.

chain.cause: Fluid particles collide with any surface they touch
chain.effect: they push on it, perpendicular to the surface, with a pressure P = F⊥/A

chain.cause: Each layer of a fluid at rest holds up the weight of the fluid above it
A column of height h of a fluid of density ρ has weight ρghA on area A
chain.effect: the pressure grows by ρgh: P = P₀ + ρgh

chain.cause: A gauge reads zero in open air
chain.effect: it measures gauge pressure, ρgh, not the absolute pressure P₀ + ρgh

ideas: Pressure is perpendicular force per area, P = F⊥/A, in pascals (1 Pa = 1 N/m²). It is a scalar: the force it makes on any surface points straight into that surface.
In a fluid at rest, P = P₀ + ρgh. Pressure depends only on depth, not on the container's shape or the amount of fluid.
Absolute pressure P includes the atmosphere's P₀ ≈ 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa. Gauge pressure P − P₀ = ρgh is what a gauge or tire gauge reads.
About 10 m of water adds one atmosphere of pressure.

misconception.wrong: Pressure is a force, so it points down, and more water in a container means more pressure at the bottom.
misconception.right: Pressure is force per area, a scalar. It acts equally in every direction at a point, and at the bottom of a container it depends only on the depth: P = P₀ + ρgh.

summary: Pressure is perpendicular force per area, a scalar in pascals; in a fluid at rest the absolute pressure is P = P₀ + ρgh, set only by depth, and the gauge pressure (what gauges read) is ρgh.
